highlights: Documented as a feudal manor from 1200; rebuilt as a Baroque summer residence from 1726 by Count Carlo Giacinto Roero
Piedmontese Baroque architecture influenced by Filippo Juvarra, friend and mentor to the count
Visited by the King and Queen of Sardinia in 1773
Converted into a luxury hotel in 2011; retains a small history museum and the elliptical Chapel of Santa Teresa
description:
Castello di Guarene stands on the site of a feudal manor documented as early as 1200, in the Roero hills of Piedmont — a landscape later inscribed as part of the UNESCO wine-growing heritage of the region. In 1726, Count Carlo Giacinto Roero began an extensive reconstruction, transforming the medieval manor into a Baroque summer residence with architecture influenced by Filippo Juvarra, the celebrated architect who was both friend and mentor to the count. The prestige of the completed residence drew royal attention: the King and Queen of Sardinia visited in 1773.

Ownership passed to the Provana di Collegno family in 1899, and the castle remained a private residence until 2011, when new owners acquired the property and converted it into a luxury hotel. Today's 12 rooms and suites — eight on the third floor named after historical figures, four on the ground floor — occupy the historic Baroque building itself, ranging from a 40-square-meter Classic Room to a 200-square-meter Luxury Suite, alongside the estate's elliptical-plan Chapel of Santa Teresa and a small museum dedicated to the castle's history.

Filippo Juvarra's influence on the 1726 reconstruction connects Guarene to one of the defining figures of the Piedmontese Baroque, whose broader body of work reshaped the architectural identity of the House of Savoy's territory during the same period.

The 1773 visit by the King and Queen of Sardinia marks the moment the Roero family's summer residence reached the height of its social prestige, a peak the building's later 19th- and 20th-century private ownership under the Provana di Collegno family maintained without the same public visibility.

The 2011 conversion into a hotel preserved rather than replaced the building's Baroque character, with today's 12 rooms distributed across the same structure the count completed nearly three centuries earlier — no modern annex was added to accommodate the property's new hospitality function.

The surrounding Roero and neighboring Langhe hills, both UNESCO-listed wine landscapes, give guests staying at Guarene direct access to one of Italy's most celebrated wine regions, with the town of Alba a short drive away for its own historic center and white-truffle tradition.

faqs.question: Are all the rooms at Guarene Castle within the historic building?
faqs.answer: Yes — all 12 rooms and suites are within the 18th-century Baroque building itself, eight on the third floor and four on the ground floor.

faqs.question: Can I visit Guarene Castle without staying overnight?
faqs.answer: No confirmed independent day-visit product was found; the castle's small history museum and chapel are part of the hotel experience for overnight guests.

faqs.question: How large are the rooms at Guarene Castle?
faqs.answer: Room sizes vary considerably, from a 40-square-meter Classic Room to a 200-square-meter Luxury Suite.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** About 10 minutes by car from Alba; roughly 1h from Turin and 1h30 from Genoa.

**Rooms & rates:** 12 rooms and suites, all within the historic 18th-century Baroque building — 8 on the third floor, 4 on the ground floor.

**On-site:** Restaurant, gardens, on-site history museum, the elliptical Chapel of Santa Teresa.

**Good to know:** Room sizes vary dramatically, from a 40m² Classic Room to a 200m² Luxury Suite — worth checking the specific room category if space is a priority.

**Combine with:** The Roero and Langhe wine regions, both UNESCO-listed landscapes, and the town of Alba.
